title: `substring` positions and lengths are `INT`: wider ones raise (ANSI) or wrap
verdict: `substring_range`: a `BIGINT` past 32 bits raises `CAST_OVERFLOW` (ANSI) or wraps
description: `substring`'s position and length are `INT`; a `BIGINT` argument is cast. Under ANSI 4294967297 (2³² + 1) raises `CAST_OVERFLOW`; without ANSI it wraps to 1 (`substring('hello', 4294967297, 2)` is `he`). Any value from 2³¹ to 2³² raises under ANSI where the reference computes.
Within `INT`, the end of the window is clamped to the `int` range: `substring('héllo', 2, 2147483647)` is `éllo`.
reference: `substring_range`: offsets outside `[-2³², 2³²)` raise (#336). Spark under ANSI raises from 2³¹ on, a stricter range: an extra raise where the reference returns a string.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `substr('Spark SQL', 5)` has the length `2147483647` (an `int`) in its schema and returns `k SQL`: the window's end is clamped (ANSI on)

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.

notes: `python -m sverify_dev.spark_fuzz --rows 300 --seed 738`: random rows leaning on the fact's edges, each construct run with spark.sql.ansi.enabled on and off, on the folded and the codegen path, and compared with a model of this fact (value, result type, error class). 794 of 794 results as the fact says.
substring_range[0]: 300 rows, `substring(s, p, l)`, 794 of 794 results as the fact says (raised: CAST_OVERFLOW 30).
Spark 4.3.0, Java 21.0.12.1, Linux amd64, local[2], session time zone UTC.
